Assertion (A): "Trade with Rome flourished in the post-Satavahana era." This statement is false. Indo-Roman trade reached its peak during the Satavahana period (1st Century BCE–2nd Century CE). After the decline of the Roman Empire in the West and the fall of the Satavahanas, trade with Rome gradually declined. Although overseas trade continued with Southeast Asia and other regions, Roman trade no longer flourished during the post-Satavahana period.
Reason (R): "No ruler had issued coins with ship motif after Satavahanas." This statement is true. The Satavahanas were famous for issuing coins bearing the ship motif, symbolising their active maritime trade. No later Andhra dynasty is known to have issued coins featuring this motif. Since the Assertion is false and the Reason is true, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: What were the gold coins called during the Kakatiya period?

Other coins included: • Ruka – Silver coin • Veesam – Fractional denomination The circulation of these coins reflects the flourishing economy and active inland as well as overseas trade under the Kakatiyas.
